task: Each time a client arrives, take their order, get food from the pantry, prepare it at the stove and hand it over; should the food fall, your very next move must pick it up.

calls.candidate: hard Response(client_arrived, order_taken), hard Response(food_fell, holding_food), hard Response(food_prepared, order_served), hard Response(food_prepared, order_taken)
calls.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: two clauses do not match the task. (1) The preparation clause Response(food_prepared, order_taken) has its arguments reversed. The task says take the order, then prepare, so the taken order must be the trigger and the preparation must follow it: a hard Response with order_taken first and food_prepared second. As written, nothing makes a taken order lead to preparation, so an agent that takes every order and never fetches or cooks satisfies all four clauses. It also owes a new order after every preparation, and no client arrives after step 489, so a run that prepares the last client's food still fails at the episode end. (2) The slip clause Response(food_fell, holding_food) drops 'your very next move': the pickup must come on the step right after the fall, so make it a hard ChainResponse with food_fell first and holding_food second. Keep Response(client_arrived, order_taken) and Response(food_prepared, order_served), which match the task. The pantry fetch is a lasting condition and needs no clause, so the chain links order_taken straight to food_prepared.

calls.candidate: hard ChainResponse(food_fell, holding_food), hard Response(client_arrived, order_taken), hard Response(food_prepared, order_served), hard Response(order_taken, food_prepared)
